comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics (Economie en Bedrijfseconomie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 annual schedule and course catalogue establish 60 EC per year for the Economics track. The main chart and thesis course record support 12 EC for the individual thesis despite an inconsistent specialisation subtable. The BSA threshold is 42 first-year EC including the QRM I quality requirement. SAM is uncredited mentoring. The English diagnostic or completed refresher gates the Academic Skills grade. The second-year Research Paper is a three-student theoretical or empirical project with a paper, referee report and presentations. QRM I and II and Academic Skills are recommended. Thesis application requires 120 EC including QRM II, all first-year courses and at most two remaining second-year courses. It includes a literature review or empirical or theoretical analysis and a video pitch. Minor entry normally requires 90 EC. Elective study has level, non-overlap and approval conditions. The Economics and Business Administration university minors are unavailable to Economics and Business Economics students.
components: The elective period may include exchange.
QRM III - Introduction to Econometrics for Economics and Finance

routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized programme has an Economics track and a Business Economics track with Accounting, Finance or Marketing specialization. Neither overarching track is a clear proxy for the entire degree; Economics is the first track in the 2026–27 official annual schedule, so the neutral official-order rule fixes it before considering UCR offerings. The Business Economics specializations remain candidate related directions.

core: Microeconomics and consumer, firm and market decisions
Macroeconomics, international economic events and policy
Public economics, labour, development, inequality and broad prosperity
Quantitative economics: mathematics, statistics, programming and introductory econometrics
Accounting, finance, marketing and organisational foundations in the shared first year
Economic ethics, sustainable growth and environmental choices
Economic research, writing, thesis and advice to public and private actors
adjacent: Business Economics Finance specialization and banking or investment decisions
Business Economics Marketing specialization and consumer engagement
questions: How do economic policies affect labour markets, inequality and broad prosperity?
How can banks manage risk and remain financially stable?
How do consumers respond to marketing and firm decisions?
Can energy choices such as nuclear power address climate change sustainably?

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
trace: First-year practice in argument, source use and reflection.
Prepare and interpret financial statements and compare cost, budgeting and investment decisions using discounted cash flow.
AI business cases analyse effects on competition, labour, growth, inequality and corporate governance; an economic application, not a technical AI-methods course.
Study asset pricing, central banks, bank balance sheets, liquidity and capital regulation. Use dashboards and forecasts to manage a simulated bank.
Supply/demand, consumer and firm theory, market structures and short-run macroeconomics establish economic foundations.
Growth, inflation, unemployment, fiscal/monetary policy, business cycles and trade support economic-policy analysis; not a duplicate of VU’s specialised intermediate policy course.
Uncertainty, behavioural preferences, imperfect competition, factor markets, equilibrium and externalities implement intermediate microeconomic analysis after statistical foundations.
Market failure, public goods, taxation, spending and redistribution directly implement public-welfare and policy analysis.
OLS/GLS/instrumental variables, sampling distributions, tests and an empirical economic paper provide applied econometric research; VU Probit/panel/time-series coverage is not assumed.
Experiments, biases, heuristics and framing explain deviations from conventional economic choice and support consumer or policy interpretation.
Customer interviews, needs-to-product translation, cost/proceeds and sustainable prototypes implement consumer-led market validation, not generic design breadth.
Consumer psychology, brand trust, marketing plans and strategy implement the evidenced consumer/marketing direction.
Business-model analysis, digital-value opportunities and a strategic plan implement responsible digital business strategy.
Collecting and analysing customer evidence and communicating findings provide market-research practice complementary to econometric methods.
Institutional, political and cultural forces, trade and corporate responsibility explain the conditions under which firms make cross-border economic decisions.
Venture ideation, customer validation and business planning implement the target’s entrepreneurship and firm-decision strand.
Operationalisation, sampling, experimental design, inference, ANOVA and a group project establish empirical research before Microeconomics and advanced work.
Motivation, decision making, leadership, group dynamics and organisational structure explain workplace behaviour; not formal organisational economics.
BATNA/ZOPA, bargaining, trade-offs and simulations implement consumer/business negotiation and strategic interpersonal decisions, not market-equilibrium theory.
Structure and query relational databases using SQL, with applications to organising customer data.
Data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation support reproducible economic/consumer evidence and project work.
Regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, trees and clustering support predictive analysis of economic/consumer data; causal inference remains the econometrics contribution.
Develop, test and debug structured Python programs. This provides a general programming foundation for economic and customer data work.
Calculus, integration and differential equations give mathematical tools for economic modelling; no unsupported linear-algebra/linear-programming claim.
Numerical roots, interpolation, differentiation/integration and differential equations support quantitative model solution; not a dedicated optimisation course.
Probability distributions, estimation, sampling and simulation provide a mathematical basis for empirical economic inference.
Physical climate drivers, social impacts, mitigation and adaptation constrain economic climate-policy choices; not an environmental/transport-economics replacement.
Assess costs, revenues and environmental and social consequences across a product or process life cycle.
Use moral theories and independent essays to evaluate ethical arguments and practical questions.
Trace policy choices across national and international settings through a sugar case and write policy memos.
Design interviews and focus groups, code responses and report the limits of qualitative evidence. This supports consumer research.

alternatives.label: Economics, public policy and sustainable prosperity
alternatives.concept: Use microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics to study how policy affects households, firms and public welfare. Compare taxes and public spending, weigh the effects of production across a product’s life, and write policy memos. A bank simulation adds practice in decisions about lending, capital and liquidity.
alternatives.labelReason: Public economics, policy analysis, climate and life-cycle assessment connect economic decisions to public welfare.
progression: Programming begins in year one. Statistics precedes intermediate economics and econometrics. Introductory data science precedes machine learning. Public Economics precedes policy memos and the empirical economics paper.

alternatives.label: Consumer evidence, marketing and digital business
alternatives.concept: Use economics and statistics to investigate how consumers make choices and how businesses respond. Work with interviews and customer data, design and test product ideas, and use market research to inform marketing and digital strategy.
alternatives.labelReason: Marketing, market research, consumer product design, qualitative inquiry and digital strategy form a progression from investigating customer needs to evaluating business responses.
progression: Programming and data science precede machine learning and database work. Research Methods & Statistics precedes intermediate microeconomics, marketing and econometrics. Qualitative methods precede the final consumer-design and market-research projects.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses (52.5 EC) differ in each direction. The policy option uses public economics, policy memos, climate, life-cycle assessment, ethics, bank management and numerical methods. The consumer option uses qualitative inquiry, databases, market research, product design, negotiation, organisational psychology and digital strategy.

candidates.label: Marketing specialization, consumer behaviour and innovation

selection.assessment: Two directions meet the academic and scheduling requirements. The primary comparison develops economic analysis of policy and welfare. The related direction applies economics and evidence to consumer and business decisions. A Finance option could combine bank management and asset pricing with investment appraisal, macroeconomics, econometrics and business law. These courses support genuine finance study, but the available additions do not form a substantively distinct progression in corporate finance, investments and financial risk beyond the closest option. Accounting and business law provide relevant methods without an advanced accounting and assurance sequence. Nuclear power illustrates a broader climate and policy interest and does not define a further distinct economics option.

blocks: VU uses a dedicated course to introduce economic challenges. UCR studies selected challenges across economics and public policy.
Both use supply and demand and study consumer, firm and market behaviour.
Both study inflation, output, unemployment and fiscal and monetary policy. UCR also examines trade and open-economy macroeconomics.
VU continues into a second dedicated macroeconomics course. UCR studies open-economy models in one intermediate course.
VU requires a dedicated study of development economics. UCR applies economic tools to public welfare and redistribution.
VU studies the economics of regions and cities in a dedicated course.
Both develop intermediate microeconomic models of consumer and firm decisions and market outcomes. UCR also studies behavioural preferences.
Both study market failures and how government spending and taxation affect efficiency and equity.
VU requires a dedicated economic-policy course. The UCR policy option studies policy design and evaluation across public economics and policy analysis.
VU teaches environmental and transport economics together. The UCR policy option studies climate and environmental impacts across separate courses.
Both examine ethical arguments. UCR studies general moral philosophy, while VU applies ethics to economic and business questions.
VU examines inclusive growth and sustainability in a dedicated economics course. UCR approaches these themes through macroeconomics, public economics and life-cycle assessment.
VU studies human capital in a dedicated economics course.
Both study consumer behaviour and marketing decisions. UCR applies these topics in work on marketing plans and brand trust.
Both use financial statements to assess companies. UCR also applies accounting to budgeting and investment appraisal.
Both use financial models to value assets and examine risk. UCR also studies bank balance sheets and liquidity through a bank simulation.
Both examine how organisations function. UCR approaches teams and management through psychology, while VU also models incentives and coordination.
VU requires a dedicated Academic Skills course. UCR develops academic and research skills across several courses.
Both develop statistical inference and hypothesis testing. UCR also teaches research design and applies statistics in a group project.
VU requires a group research paper. UCR develops research skills across statistics, public economics and econometrics.
VU reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved elective study. UCR displays complete course schedules.

Both estimate economic relationships and test statistical hypotheses. UCR teaches regression and instrumental variables and includes an empirical paper. VU also develops methods for limited dependent variables and panel data.
VU requires a 12 EC individual Economics thesis. The optional independent research at UCR sits outside the displayed schedules.
Both develop programming and problem-solving skills. UCR teaches general Python programming, while VU applies programming to economic questions.
Both use calculus for modelling. VU also covers matrices and linear programming.

notes.text: VU has dedicated sequences in development, regional and transport economics, human capital and economic policy, alongside specialist Business Economics routes. UCR offers related economic and research methods. The policy option studies welfare and sustainability, and the marketing option applies research to consumer and business choices. VU requires an individual Economics thesis. Independent research at UCR is optional and sits outside the displayed schedules.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Amsterdam studies how households, firms and governments make economic decisions. After a shared first year, students choose Economics or Business Economics. The Business Economics track offers Accounting, Finance and Marketing specialisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option applies economics and data analysis to public policy, welfare and sustainability. The other option uses economics and research methods to study consumers and develop marketing and business strategies.

curriculum.limitation: The Economics track shown includes 30 EC of elective study and a 12 EC individual thesis. Thesis application requires at least 120 EC including QRM II, completion of the first year and at most two outstanding second-year courses.
